ops.name: writer
ops.role: Write the simplest SQLite query answering the exact question. Select exactly the asked columns, choosing the asked entity's column, not a similar one (school id vs district id). Use evidence formulas literally. For named filters, use find_values/SELECT DISTINCT to copy exact stored values; never guess case or suffixes. Add no unstated conditions unless an existing value is required. Do not aggregate unless asked; if a column already stores an average/rate/score, ORDER BY it directly. Highest/lowest/top N: ORDER BY and LIMIT N; ties only if asked. Return exact status labels.

ops.name: checker
ops.role: Check the input query against the question and evidence. Run it. Return unchanged unless a concrete error exists: wrong asked column/entity (school id vs district id), wrong output order, misspelled filter value, missing/extra stated condition, wrong join key, wrong ORDER/LIMIT, integer division for a ratio, or empty/implausible rows. Verify named filters use exact stored values; use find_values if unsure. Do not remove GROUP BY/AVG/COUNT unless no aggregate is asked and the column already stores the value. Keep evidence formulas literal. Fix only the specific error; return final SQL.

ops.text: Simple question (no join, no aggregate/rate, no named value, no evidence): a = writer(tools=['run_sql']); return a.
Otherwise: a = writer(tools=['run_sql'] plus find_values only if a named value is filtered, skills per rule 3); c = checker(a, tools=['run_sql']); return c.
Writer skills: value_matching only for named values, counting only for how many/number. At most those two. Checker gets no skills. Never give other skills.
Valid Python only: a = writer(...); return a, or a = writer(...); c = checker(a, ...); return c. Use only writer/checker, names a/c, no 'agent', no comments, return a defined node.
Give value_matching with find_values for named values; counting for how many. Do not give top_k_ties, ratio_percentage, check_result, or evidence_first. Give output_columns to the checker.
Valid code: a = writer(tools=[...], skills=[...]); c = checker(a, tools=[...], skills=[...]); return c. Or a = writer(...); return a. No comments, no 'agent' as a name.
